payload: The Cybertruck is now a leading candidate for the biggest automobile failure ever: against Musk's on-camera prediction of roughly 250,000 and 'maybe 500,000' a year, it didn't crack 40,000 sales in its first year (which had years of pre-orders baked in) and only about 7,100 have been registered in the US in the first half of this year — with those numbers propped up by Musk selling Cybertrucks to his own companies (20% of Q4 sales went to SpaceX). Futurism compares it to Ford's Edsel (introduced 1957, discontinued after 2 years; projected ~200,000, sold under a third), long cited as America's biggest auto disaster, and concludes the Cybertruck is actually worse on projected-versus-actual sales. The creator's diagnosis: like Homer Simpson designing his own car, Musk built what he wanted, priced it far above the $40,000 he had promised, and tanked the company's reputation, when buyers just wanted a reasonably priced EV.
notes: Sales/comparison figures attributed to a Futurism piece; Musk's 250k-500k prediction is played from an old clip of him.
Framed as opinion commentary tied to Tesla's declining stock.
